title: Long TSLA — Q2 Earnings Binary; Enter July 23 Open Only If Gross Margin Exceeds 15%
entry: DO NOT ENTER TODAY (July 21) — morning briefing explicitly flags TSLA pre-earnings as a 'Don't Buy.' Enter ONLY on July 23 open if Q2 FY2026 gross margin (reported July 22 after market close) exceeds 15.0%. Options market implies a 7.6% swing on earnings; conditional entry accepts the risk only when the gross margin catalyst confirms the bull thesis. If margin is above 15%: enter at the July 23 open in the range $350–$395 (adjusting for AH reaction). Do NOT initiate above $400 (above that level AH gap has already captured most of the margin re-rating move). Do NOT enter if Q2 gross margin is below 15.0% regardless of delivery beat or EPS — the margin signal is the only credible catalyst for a sustained move.
stop_loss: $325 daily close (~12% below $369.57 reference price; will be updated after entry on July 23) — at $325, either (1) Q2 gross margin was a one-quarter beat driven by mix shift (higher-margin Model X/S deliveries vs lower-margin Model Y/3 in Q3 guide), meaning the sustainability of margin recovery is in doubt; (2) Q3 gross margin guidance implies deceleration back below 14.5%; (3) macro STEP ASIDE regime is overwhelming the individual catalyst. For reference: 12% stop from $369.57 = $325.40; if entry is at a different level on July 23, adjust the stop to 12% below actual entry.
targets: $400 — Options-implied 7.6% upside from $369.57 = $397.70; initial market reaction captures the margin beat; sell-side begins revising FY2026 gross margin estimates toward 16%; AH gap confirms sustained margin trajectory; cover 40% of conditional position; +8.2% gain from $369.57 reference

$440 — Full gross margin re-rating: sell-side consensus reaches 15.5%–16.5% for H2 FY2026; TSLA Robotaxi launch timeline confirmed for Austin (Q4 FY2026 or Q1 FY2027) adds optionality premium to the stock; energy storage segment (Megapack) records second consecutive quarterly gross margin above 30%; $440 = 100x FY2026 FCF at modestly higher FCF trajectory; cover 40% of remaining position; +19.1% gain

$480 — Blue-sky case: Robotaxi commercial deployment confirmed, Optimus robot deliveries accelerate to 10K+/month run rate by end of FY2026, TSLA gross margin reaches 17%+ by Q3; at $480 TSLA trades at ~20% premium to current price with a legitimate robotics/AI valuation floor that is separate from the auto business; hold final 20% into Q3 FY2026 earnings; +30.0% gain
risk_reward: 1:2.5 to Target 3 from $369.57 reference (risk $44.57; T3 reward $110.43)
catalyst: Tesla Q2 FY2026 earnings report after market close July 22. The known positive: 480K deliveries were already disclosed on July 2, beating consensus of approximately 455K — the delivery beat is fully priced into the current $369.57 level. The unknown binary is gross margin. Q1 FY2026 gross margin was 12.5% — the lowest in several years, driven by price cuts to maintain delivery volume. The bull case requires Q2 gross margin >15%, signaling that TSLA's pricing power has stabilized and cost-reduction programs (automation, manufacturing efficiency) are delivering. Wall Street consensus for Q2 gross margin is approximately 13.5%–14.0%; a print above 15% would be a 100–150bps beat with positive forward implications. Secondary catalysts: Robotaxi deployment timeline update (Austin commercial launch expected Q4 FY2026), Optimus robot production update, and Q3 guidance commentary on energy storage margins.
thesis:
Tesla is a two-part valuation problem: an auto business with a deteriorating gross margin trajectory trading on legacy tech multiples, and an optionality business (Robotaxi, Optimus, energy storage) with uncertain but potentially enormous TAMs. The conditional entry structure of this opportunity isolates the auto margin part of the problem — because without confirmed margin recovery, the optionality premium is unsupported and the stock at 100x trailing earnings is not defensible in a STEP ASIDE macro regime.

If Q2 gross margin comes in above 15%, the investment thesis shifts materially. A 15% gross margin on ~480K deliveries implies TSLA has (1) stabilized the margin drag from the Model 3/Y price cuts that began in early 2023, (2) benefited from manufacturing cost reductions at Gigafactories in Nevada and Austin, and/or (3) shifted mix toward higher-margin products (Cybertruck, Model X/S, Megapack). Any of these is durable rather than transient. At 15%+ gross margin, consensus revisions push FY2026 gross margin estimates toward 15.5%–16%, which triggers a sell-side upgrade cycle and institutional accumulation.

The 2% position size reflects the conditional structure and the high optionality nature of the trade. If the gross margin confirmation does not materialize (below 15%), do NOT enter — the miss eliminates the catalyst and the STEP ASIDE regime's 30Y above 5% / VIX above 18 environment means the stock will not rerate on delivery beats alone. The tail risk is that Musk provides positive Robotaxi commentary that creates a separate non-margin catalyst (which would also be positive), but do not enter pre-earnings on speculation of that commentary.

The counter-party argues: (1) TSLA's gross margins cannot durably recover above 15% because the Model 3/Y volume mix (which is price-competitive and thin-margin) is now 85% of deliveries; (2) Robotaxi will face regulatory delays in Austin; (3) TSLA at $369 already prices in a gross margin recovery that has not occurred. These are valid reasons this is low conviction (2% position) with a tight 12% stop.
bull_case: Q2 gross margin reports at 16.2% — 220bps above consensus of 14.0%. Stock gaps up 10–12% AH on July 22 to $410–$415. On July 23, enter at $400–$405. Sell-side immediately upgrades FY2026 gross margin to 16% and initiates a buy cycle. TSLA reaches $440 by August 8 ahead of Q3 guidance confirmation. Robotaxi Austin deployment confirmed for October 2026, adding further premium.
bear_case: Q2 gross margin comes in at 13.8% — below the 14% consensus and below the 15% trigger. Do NOT enter on July 23. Stock falls 5–8% on delivery-beat-plus-margin-miss disappointment. The conditional structure means zero capital is at risk. If somehow entered before margin confirmation, exit at $325 stop.
invalidation: Q2 gross margin below 15.0% (do not enter — the conditional trigger is not met); OR $325 daily close post-entry; OR TSLA issues Q3 gross margin guidance explicitly below 14% on the July 22 earnings call (forward deceleration thesis confirmed); OR Elon Musk announces material organizational restructuring that creates execution risk on Robotaxi or Optimus timelines
